column1: # D3 streams every texture from the CPKs into memory pools through the CPU; without these the host treats
# them as GPU-written and binds a freshly zeroed MTL texture (all textures black, only font text visible).
# Background artwork is covered at draw time using loading_art below. The complete
# frame must never be resized by a delayed probe: that also scales the text and can
# carry the loading crop into the first gameplay frames.
# The soft-edge additive light shader samples the screen through a UBO that is rewritten once per light. On the
# deferred-uniform path its 1464-vertex draw intermittently used stale screen-transform data and copied a wrong screen
# rectangle over the lantern. End the pass before this single draw so its uniforms land first; the rest of the frame
# keeps deferred uniforms, 60 fps and the normal glow.
# D3 imports nvnCommandBufferSetRenderEnableConditional / ReportCounter / ResetCounter (found in main's import names), so it
# wraps work in conditional blocks like Tears of the Kingdom does. With this off, a timestamp report's counter field carries the
# time instead of 0 (the real GPU puts the time in the second field), so the game's "counter == counter" comparisons never hold and
# every conditional clear / draw runs anyway: wasted GPU work (frame drops with many monsters) and clears the game wanted skipped.
# OFF: with conditional rendering evaluated, a light glow quad near a lantern flickered (its query result alternates), which the
# player saw as a small patch blinking. Without it every conditional clear / draw runs, which costs some GPU in heavy fights, but
# nothing is skipped on the strength of a query value we may have counted wrong.
# Exact XTX payload fingerprints for loading paintings and their side panels.
# Enlarge these background draws only; keep all loading text at its authored size.
